postgresql.name: PostgreSQL
postgresql.summary: A free, community-run database with transactional schema changes, full outer join, materialized views and six index types.
postgresql.bestWhen: You are starting fresh, ship many migrations, or need materialized views or its six documented index types.
postgresql.watchOut: It needs VACUUM housekeeping, though autovacuum is on by default. If your team already runs MySQL well, switching costs real time.

mysql.name: MySQL
mysql.summary: A mature database developed by Oracle. In 8.4 the default engine is InnoDB, which follows ACID.
mysql.bestWhen: Your team, tools and hosting already run on it, or you want Oracle vendor support.
mysql.watchOut: Its manuals show no full outer join and no materialized views, and a schema change ends any open transaction. MySQL 8.0 is in Sustaining Support.

either.name: Either one works
either.summary: Both are free, mature and handle most web apps. The post found no neutral benchmark that crowns a winner.
either.bestWhen: Your needs are plain and no feature above is a must. Test your own slowest queries on both.
either.watchOut: Do not pick on speed claims. Check your version too: MySQL 8.0 is in Sustaining Support and PostgreSQL 14 ends November 12, 2026.
